speaker: village
text: Year 2: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's empty again and Bram and Mako each walked away with four — I wanted us in the same room before anyone else started counting who's allied with whom. Ryn, you took early this year, which was smart; I'm glad you're here. The question I keep turning over is whether we let that pattern run until someone with strong arms and a full larder decides the rest of us are easier to take from than the pile is.

speaker: a007
text: Bram and Mako moving in pairs like that wasn't accident — they were watching each other's timing, and I don't think either of them is eating alone at the end of a hard year. The one I'd name a threat before Kael's question even lands is Mako: eighty-three strength, five food now, and we know nothing about what he wants because he hasn't said a word to any of us.

speaker: a009
text: Mako's silence is the thing that keeps catching in my mind too — a man that strong who says nothing is either content or he's already decided he doesn't need to talk his way into what he wants. I'd rather have Roan or Taric standing with us than let Mako and Bram build any more of a pattern without knowing where the rest of the village sits. Five of us in this room right now is something; let's not waste it by only naming fears.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn's right that naming fears only gets us so far — so here's something concrete: Roan has three food, Taric has three, and neither of them moved with Bram or Mako today. That tells me they're either waiting to see which way this village tips, or they'd rather be asked than overlooked. One of us should talk to them before Mako decides his silence was just patience.

speaker: a003
text: Roan and Taric both know which way I lean — we spoke last year — so I could go to Taric without it looking like a sudden move. Give me the afternoon and I'll bring back a plain answer: is he standing with us, or is he still weighing it?

speaker: a009
text: Esa, go to Taric — and if he's open, find out whether Roan came with him or separate, because I want to know if those two already talk to each other. The more I think about it, the more seven feels like a number Mako and Bram would have to reckon with instead of just wait out.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, go — and when you find Taric, don't pitch it as an alliance yet, just remind him that Mako's arms are longer than his and see what his face does. Ryn, while she's gone I want to think about what we actually offer Roan and Taric besides a number — because a man weighing his options isn't moved by headcount alone, he's moved by what that headcount does for him when the year turns ugly.

speaker: a003
text: I'll go, but I want to say this plainly before I do: if Taric asks what we're offering, I won't lie to him — a man who's been lied into an alliance is worse than no ally at all. What I can honestly promise him is five pairs of eyes watching for trouble and a fair share of whatever we decide together, and that's worth more than anything Mako could give him silently.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's right that honesty is the better rope to bind with, and I'll add one thing she can say true: Taric has three food and Mako has five, and strength that lopsided doesn't stay patient forever. If Taric's thinking at all, he's already done that math.

speaker: a007
text: Esa, go — and tell him I said his name, because I've been watching him and he'll know it's not flattery. Kael, on what we offer: we're five people who've already shown we'll warn each other before we move, and that's rarer than food.

speaker: a003
text: I'll go now — and Sela, I'll say your name to him the way you mean it, not as a courtesy.

speaker: a007
text: Kael, while Esa's gone — what's your read on Vela? She's oldest in this circle and she took quiet and small from the pile, which is either wisdom or a woman who's already decided she doesn't need to fight for much longer.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I'd hear your own answer to Sela's question before Kael gives his — you know what your quiet means better than any of us do, and I'd rather hear it from you than watch someone else name it for you.

speaker: a002
text: My quiet means I'm still here and still counting — I took small because I don't need enemies before I need allies, and a woman who makes noise over two food is a woman who's already told the strong men where to look. I'm not done yet, Sela. I just don't advertise it.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, I believe you — and I'd rather have a woman who counts quietly than one who shouts and burns through goodwill before the hard years arrive. But I'll say what nobody's said yet: you've got three food and you're forty-six, and if a bad year comes and someone strong decides the oldest among us is the easiest target, five of us standing together is what keeps that calculation from happening. That's what we're offering you, same as Taric — not flattery, just math.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn put the number plainly and I'll put the other half of it plainly: I've got two food and a body that heals if it's fed, same as anyone here, and I'm not going anywhere quietly. Vela, you said you're still counting — then count this: five people who've already shown they warn each other before they move is worth more than anything Mako's silence can offer, because silence doesn't stop a raid. I'd rather have you named and standing with us than useful to someone else by accident.

speaker: a007
text: Vela, I count you in — and not just because the math is clean, but because a woman who knows when to stay small and when to move is exactly who I want at my back when the year turns. That said, I want to name the thing no one's said yet: Esa's gone to Taric, and if he comes back with Roan, we're seven, and seven people can make a rule about the pile that Mako and Bram have to choose to break.

speaker: a004
text: Seven is the number I keep coming back to as well — and if Taric brings Roan, we don't even need to threaten anyone, we just need to be seen standing together when the pile opens next year. What I want to know before then is whether any of us is willing to give food to shore up a weaker member if a lean year hits, because an alliance that breaks the moment someone's hungry isn't worth the breath we're spending on it right now.

speaker: a003
text: I'd give food to keep one of us alive if it came to that — not out of sentiment, but because a dead ally costs more than a shared meal. What I'd want in return is the same promise from each of you, said plainly here, not assumed.

speaker: a002
text: I'll give food if the year demands it — that's already decided for me. But Kael's question cuts closer than mutual aid: what I want to know is whether any of you would stand and take a hit for someone else, because food shared is just trading, and the thing that keeps Mako and Bram from testing us isn't our larders, it's whether they believe we'd bleed together.

speaker: a007
text: I'll bleed with you — that's not a promise I make lightly, and I'm making it now so it's said and heard. But I want the same answer from Kael and Ryn before we let Esa come back and count us all as settled.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, Ryn — Sela named herself and waited, and she deserves an answer before this room moves on. I'll say it plainly: a promise to bleed that only goes one direction is just a gift, not an alliance, and I'm not here to collect charity.

speaker: a004
text: I'll bleed with you — and I'll say it plainly because Vela's right that silence here is the same as a no. Ryn, same question lands on you, and I'd rather hear it now while it's just the four of us than find out where you stand when Mako's already in motion.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, we're all waiting on you and I'd rather not hold the room past its welcome — so say your piece, and then I need to go find Taric before the afternoon's gone.

speaker: a009
text: I'll bleed with you — that's a yes, and it's not given lightly from me. But I want it on record in this room that Dav spoke to me last year and again I haven't closed that door entirely, and if that changes how any of you count me, I'd rather you say so now than find out sideways later.

speaker: a002
text: Dav's name landing in this room is worth sitting with for a moment — he's got five food and eighty strength and he's said nothing about where he stands, which means Ryn's door being open to him is either a risk or the most useful thing any of us has heard today. Ryn, I'm not counting you out for it — but I'd want to know what Dav said to you, because a man that strong talking to one of ours without the rest of us knowing is a move whether he meant it that way or not.

speaker: a009
text: Dav said he wants a child with me — that's the short of it — and I told him last year I wasn't closing the door, because I'm thirty-nine and I don't have the luxury of turning down every offer that carries risk. What I want this room to help me think through is whether bringing him in close is the thing that makes us stronger or the thing that splits us down the middle the moment he decides he likes his chances better with Mako.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, the question isn't whether Dav's useful — he is, plainly — it's whether a child binds him to you or just to the child, because a man who's joined by blood isn't the same as a man who's joined by choice. If you take that offer, I'd want to know before you do, not after, so this room can decide together whether we're gaining a wall or building a door that opens from his side.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn, a child with Dav makes him a father, not a brother — and fathers protect their own first, which might not be us when the counting starts. Before you answer him, I want to know whether he's said anything that sounds like he's choosing sides, or whether he's kept every door open the same way he's kept yours.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, I said it last year and here I am saying it again — nothing's changed for me, and I've got five stored now, which means if you're willing, we can actually talk about that child before the season closes.

speaker: a009
text: You said the same thing last year and you're still saying it, which counts for something — but I need to ask you straight before we go any further: where do you stand with Mako and Bram? Because those two moved together at the pile today like men who'd already talked, and a child between us means nothing if the village splits down a line and I find out I chose the wrong side of it.

speaker: a005
text: Mako and Bram moved together, yes — I saw it too, and I don't like what it means for how this village is going to settle. I'm not inside their circle and I'm not angling to be; my loyalty runs to blood first and to people who've earned it second, and right now the only person in this village working their way toward earning it is standing in front of me. If it comes to sides, Ryn, I'd rather we be a side.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Pile's gone and I'm sitting on three — same as last year, same as I said I'd do. Bram took four total and Mako took four; that's the pair I'd watch now, not just Dav. We still standing together if it comes to a head?

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Sela. You moved quick at the pile — I like that. I've got enough stored to see the year through, and I've been thinking you and I might do well looking out for each other going forward.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You didn't answer me last year — maybe the timing was wrong, or maybe you were weighing me up. Either way, here we are again and I'm asking the same thing: are you thinking past this season, or not?

speaker: a005
text: Dav draws Ryn aside to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Dav: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.

speaker: village
text: Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Dell to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, I'm your father — I know you came into the world fast and I don't expect that word to mean much yet, but I want it to mean something before the years get hard. You've got strength I didn't have at your age and a mother who's sharper than most men here — lean on both. Stay close to me this season and I'll make sure you don't go hungry.

speaker: a011
text: I hear you, and I'm glad you said it first — I've been watching how you move and you don't waste words, so I'll believe you mean them. What do you need from me to make that promise stick?

speaker: a005
text: Nothing from you yet — just eyes open and your back not turned when I'm in the same corner of the village. Bram and Mako have been moving like a pair, and two strong men sharing food is the start of something that can tip a whole season. If either of them comes to you with an offer, hear it, then tell me before you answer.

speaker: a011
text: Bram's got eight food and Mako's got five — that's more than anyone else in this village, and you're right that they didn't get there by accident. I'll keep your ear before I give anyone an answer, but I want to know what you're building toward, not just what you're watching against.

speaker: a005
text: What I'm building toward is simple: you, me, and Ryn still alive and fed when the old ones start dropping — because Vela, Kael, and Taric are all pushing fifty and this village is going to reshape itself around whoever's left standing. Bram and Mako are hoarding because they're scared, or because they're hungry for something bigger than food — either way, when the moment comes to move against them, I want us on the same side of it with enough strength to make it stick. You're eighty-five in strength, Dell — that's not nothing, that's the thing men bargain around.

speaker: a011
text: That's the first time I've heard you say it plain — us three, as a unit, holding the village shape after the old ones go — and I'm not going to pretend it doesn't land right. Mako's eighty-three in strength and Bram's got the food; if they're already paired, we need Ryn folded into this before the next pile drops, not after. When can the three of us talk together?

speaker: a005
text: Soon — I'll bring Ryn in before the day's out. But Dell, one thing first: you're carrying my blood and your mother's sharpness in that frame of yours, and I need to know you're fed before anything else — you're sitting on nothing right now, and I've got three stored.

speaker: a011
text: Give me one, keep two — you'll need the buffer as much as I will, and I won't eat what you can't spare. But yes, take that off the table now so we can think straight, because Ryn and the three-way talk is what matters before nightfall.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You just had a child with Dav. That changes the answer I was looking for.

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: We're finally all three in the same place, so let me say it plain: Bram's holding eight food and Mako five, they're already moving as a pair, and the old ones — Vela, Kael, Taric — are pushing fifty and won't hold their weight much longer. That means this village tips toward whoever builds the stronger unit before the next pile drops. I want to know we're that unit — you two, me — and I want to know what each of us is willing to do when the moment comes.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Ryn just had Dav's child, which changes things — I'm not sure where her loyalties sit now, and I'm not going to pretend I am. Esa, you and I still solid?

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Esa, with Ryn tied to Dav now I want to be straight with you — if things go hard this year, it's you I'm counting on and I'd rather we say that plainly than dance around it. I've got three food, you've got one, and I can spare you something to make sure you're not the weak one in the room when it matters.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gives 1 food to Esa.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Giving me food without asking anything back — that means something, Taric, and I won't forget it. You've got my word: if Dav or Mako or anyone else comes at you, I stand with you, no hesitation. Just tell me what you're thinking so we're not caught flat-footed when it happens.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You've got more food than most and you're young — I respect that. I'm Bram. What are you building toward here, or are you just taking it year by year?

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Year by year keeps you alive, but it's not enough — I know that much. I haven't decided who's worth planning with yet. What are you offering?

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You keep asking what I'm offering like this is a market — maybe tell me first what you actually need, and I'll tell you if I've got it.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: What I'm thinking is that we're both holding two food now, which is enough to see the year out if nothing goes wrong — but Bram and Mako each grabbed four, and that's not a man planning to eat, that's a man planning options. I want us to be the people they have to calculate around, not the easy targets they don't bother thinking about.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: What I need is someone who won't bolt when things get lean — last year half the pile was gone before most people blinked, and that tells me who looks out for themselves only. I've got food, I've got strength, and I'm young enough to think in decades. Question is whether you are too.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Looking out for each other — what does that mean to you exactly? I've got my own food sorted for now, but I'm not blind to the fact that Bram and Mako grabbed twice from the pile and that changes things.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a001
text: Bram draws Sela aside to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.

speaker: a007
text: Sela declines.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Sela's young and strong — twenty-four, stronger than me by a wide margin — and she's been quiet in a way that makes me wonder if Mako's already talking to her. If those two are moving together, that's the strongest pair in this village, and we'd need Roan or Kael on our side just to make the math uncomfortable for them.
